objectives.title: Find details in a short text

lessons.explanation: A descriptive adjective agrees with its noun in number and gender. Adjectives ending in a consonant generally add -es in the plural; those ending in a vowel add -s.
commonMistakes: Pluralizing the noun alone is not enough: make the adjective plural too.
lessons.provenance: Original Palabra lesson; grammatical rules checked against RAE references. Author review, 2026-10-30; no independent teacher audit.

lessons.explanation: Ser identifies people and things, describes characteristics and gives origin. Its present forms are soy, eres, es, somos, sois, son. Description is a use, not a promise of permanence.
commonMistakes: Use son for a plural subject. Somos means we are, not they are.
lessons.provenance: Original Palabra lesson; grammatical rules checked against RAE references. Author review, 2026-10-30; no independent teacher audit.

lessons.explanation: Read the question first. Find the sentence that gives that detail, and check who, when or where it describes.
examples: ¿Cuándo? Look for the time or day.
commonMistakes: A familiar word alone may not answer the question. Check the whole message.
lessons.provenance: Original Palabra strategy lesson; author review, not an independent educator audit.

lessons.explanation: Read the question, then listen for its detail. Replay as needed. Reading the transcript makes it supported practice.
examples: Listen for names, numbers and places.

stimuli.SpanishText: En nuestra mesa hay muchas frutas. Las manzanas son rojas y las naranjas son anaranjadas. Mi hermana es deportista y come fruta todos los días. Nosotros somos estudiantes y necesitamos comida variada. Los tomates son pequeños, pero las zanahorias son grandes. Mi padre dice «El agua es importante». En casa bebemos agua con la comida y compartimos una ensalada verde. No es una receta médica; es nuestra comida de hoy.
stimuli.provenance: Original fictional passage, authored for Palabra. Not a textbook reading.
